title: Trump Warns of a 'Heavy Hit' on Iran as Tankers Burn in Hormuz; Talks Described as Stalled
dek: Trump says the US must do 'something large' after the midterms, while Iran says four tankers struck mines in the strait and its negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Aerial view of the Strait of Hormuz

keyPoints: Trump told Fox News the US 'has to do something large' against Iran and that any action could involve a 'heavy hit'. Reports say US strike plans were ready as early as Wednesday.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four oil tankers that tried to cross south of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines and were still burning. Meridian has not independently verified this claim.
Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X that Americans said 'NO TO WAR' in the midterms.
Bloomberg reported Tehran and Washington were reviewing new mediator proposals after limited US strikes, and Qatari mediators had visited Tehran.
body:
The risk of a new US-Iran military confrontation rose on Wednesday morning, with Trump threatening a major strike and Iran's Revolutionary Guards reporting ships destroyed in the Strait of Hormuz.

## Trump's warning

In a Fox News interview, Trump said the US "has to do something large" in response to Iran, and that any action could involve a "heavy hit." He also said Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon." Gulf News reported that US officials said strike plans were ready from as early as Wednesday. Earlier, US forces carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, which officials described as defensive.

Trump also acknowledged that the Iran war had played some role in the Republican losses in the midterm elections. He told Fox News, "I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I've done with Iran."

## Hormuz

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four "non-compliant" oil tankers attempting to pass a prohibited route south of the Strait of Hormuz were destroyed after striking naval mines, and that they were still burning. The Guards also said two other vessels had been halted and that a drone was shot down over the strait. Gulf News and CBS News reported these claims. Meridian has not independently confirmed the tanker losses, and no ship-tracking or shipping-company confirmation is included in this story.

Tehran claims control of the strait and has targeted vessels that cross without its authorization since the war began.

## Talks

Bloomberg reported that Iran and the US were reviewing the latest proposals from mediators to avoid a return to all-out war. A diplomat briefed on the matter said Qatari mediators traveled to Tehran on Monday and that the talks there were positive. ABC News and Gulf News described talks between the two countries as stalled.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was seeking dialogue and that renewed war would benefit no one. Ghalibaf said Americans voted "NO TO WAR" in the midterm elections, and he said Iran endorsed that message. A senior Iranian figure told CBS News that the US response to the latest proposal was "not convincing" and that Iran's demands, including a halt to fighting across the region, must be met for the strait to reopen.

Meridian will update this story if the US strikes, if the tanker reports are confirmed by independent sources, or if mediators announce a new proposal.
